A1-g0-C1.title: Asymmetric sigmoid MIL for mask-free MVFA segmentation adapters
A1-g0-C1.summary: Train MVFA's segmentation adapters from image labels only: every patch of a normal image is pushed to the normal anchor and the top-1% patches of an abnormal image to the abnormal anchor, with a SigLIP-style sigmoid loss at all four levels.
A1-g0-C1.research_idea: Independent variable: segmentation supervision (Dice+Focal on masks; symmetric top-k BCE MIL as in the problem; asymmetric sigmoid MIL). For level l and patch j, z_j = t (cos(f_j, T_abn) - cos(f_j, T_nor)) + b with learnable t, b. Normal image: mean over all patches of softplus(z_j). Abnormal image: mean over the top-k patches (k = 1% of patches, at least 3) of softplus(-z_j), plus 0.1 x mean over the bottom 50% of softplus(z_j) (most of an abnormal image is normal tissue). Dependent variables: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on the held-out modality, and retention = (AUROC_MIL - 0.5)/(AUROC_mask - 0.5).
A1-g0-C1.hypothesis: Asymmetric sigmoid MIL on image labels from all five source datasets retains at least 75% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and exceeds the symmetric top-k BCE MIL of the problem statement by at least 2 pixel-AUROC points.
A1-g0-C1.rationale: A normal image carries a pixel-level label for free: every patch is normal. Only abnormal images are ambiguous. The problem's symmetric top-k MIL wastes this: a normal image constrains only its k most anomalous patches. An asymmetric objective supervises all patches of normal images and only the most anomalous patches of abnormal images, with MadCLIP's sigmoid patch-text loss, which tolerates the many-to-one patch/anchor relation.
A1-g0-C1.method: 1) loss.py: add asym_mil_loss(seg_patch_tokens, text_features, label, t, b, k_frac=0.01) computing per-level cosines (tokens L2-normalised as in MVFA), the normal-all-patches term and the abnormal top-k term with the bottom-50% term; sum over the four levels with MVFA's level weights. 2) train_zero.py: replace the seg branch's Focal+Dice block (executed only when the dataset has masks) by asym_mil_loss for every image; t (init 10) and b (init -5) are nn.Parameters in the seg optimizer; detection branch unchanged. 3) Hyper-parameters: Adam, lr and epochs as in the released script, batch size 1 as in the code; k_frac in {0.5%, 1%, 2%}; bottom-term weight 0.1. 4) Inference unchanged (test_zero.py).
A1-g0-C1.experiment: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; symmetric top-k BCE MIL (the problem's operator). Ablations: k_frac; bottom-50% term on/off; sigmoid vs. BCE-on-probabilities; which levels receive the loss. Falsified if retention is below 60% or there is no gain over symmetric MIL.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g0-C2.title: MIL-to-mask self-distillation with cross-level agreement
A1-g0-C2.summary: First train the segmentation adapters with the problem's top-k MIL, then convert their multi-level maps on abnormal source images into pseudo-masks (patches anomalous at three or more levels) and retrain with MVFA's Dice and Focal losses on those pseudo-masks.
A1-g0-C2.research_idea: Independent variable: segmentation supervision (true masks; top-k MIL only; MIL followed by one or two rounds of pseudo-mask self-distillation). Round 0: top-k MIL (k = 1%) on all source images. Pseudo-mask of an abnormal source image: patches in the image-wise top 5% at >= 3 of the 4 levels, upsampled with nearest neighbour; normal images get empty masks; pixels of abnormal images outside the pseudo-mask but above the image median are ignored in the Focal term. Rounds 1-2: Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities; pseudo-mask precision and recall against true masks on BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC source images (analysis only).
A1-g0-C2.hypothesis: One round of MIL-to-mask self-distillation increases held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points over MIL alone, and cross-level agreement (>= 3 levels) yields pseudo-masks with at least 1.5x the precision of deepest-level pseudo-masks.
A1-g0-C2.rationale: MIL supervises only the top patches and gives fragmented maps, but its maps on abnormal source images contain coarse localisation. Turning the MIL-trained maps into pseudo-masks with cross-level agreement and training the segmentation adapters on them with MVFA's own Dice and Focal losses (self-distillation) can densify the supervision while still never using an expert mask.
A1-g0-C2.method: 1) Round 0 as in the problem statement (loss.py: topk_mil). 2) New script make_pseudo_masks.py: run the round-0 seg branch on all source training images, compute per-level probability maps, apply the agreement rule, save masks and ignore maps as .npy. 3) dataset/medical_zero.py: load pseudo-masks for every source dataset (seg_idx >= 0 for all six). 4) train_zero.py round 1: existing Focal + Dice with an ignore weight map. 5) Optional round 2 regenerates pseudo-masks from the round-1 model. Hyper-parameters: top 5%, agreement >= 3 levels, released learning rate and epochs per round.
A1-g0-C2.experiment: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; MIL only. Ablations: agreement threshold (2, 3, 4 levels); top percentage (2%, 5%, 10%); number of rounds. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over MIL only.
provenance: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g0-C3.title: DINOv2-affinity propagation of MIL evidence into pseudo-masks
A1-g0-C3.summary: Refine the MIL-trained patch maps of abnormal source images by propagation over a frozen DINOv2 patch-affinity graph and use the result as pseudo-masks for MVFA's Dice and Focal losses.
A1-g0-C3.research_idea: Independent variable: pseudo-mask refinement (none; DINOv2 affinity propagation; CLIP-feature affinity propagation). Stage 1: top-k MIL (problem statement). Stage 2: for each abnormal source image, DINOv2 ViT-S/14 patch features on a grid matched to MVFA's, affinity A_ij = max(0, cos)^8, row-normalised; m' = (0.7 A + 0.3 I)^3 m; pseudo-mask = m' > 0.5 max(m'). Stage 3: Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks. Dependent variables: pseudo-mask IoU (analysis), pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities.
A1-g0-C3.hypothesis: DINOv2-refined pseudo-masks increase held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points over the unrefined MIL maps and over CLIP-affinity propagation, while image AUROC changes by less than 1 point.
A1-g0-C3.rationale: Image-level MIL localises a handful of the most anomalous patches. DINO features are spatially coherent, so a random walk over a DINO patch-affinity graph can grow MIL evidence into region-shaped pseudo-masks that supervise MVFA's segmentation adapters densely, with DINO used only offline during training.
A1-g0-C3.method: 1) Stage 1: loss.py topk_mil in train_zero.py. 2) New script refine_masks.py: torch.hub DINOv2 ViT-S/14 (frozen), patch features resized to MVFA's patch grid, affinity and propagation in torch; save masks. 3) Stage 3: existing Focal + Dice on pseudo-masks for every source image (normal: empty). 4) DINO is not used at test time; inference cost unchanged. 5) Hyper-parameters: alpha 0.7, beta 8, t 3 (ablation alpha {0.5, 0.7, 0.9}, t {1, 3, 5}).
A1-g0-C3.experiment: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; MIL only; CLIP-affinity propagation. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over MIL only.
provenance: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

A1-g0-C4.title: Hybrid supervision: synthetic-lesion masks plus real-image MIL
A1-g0-C4.summary: Train the segmentation adapters with Dice + Focal on synthetic lesions pasted into normal source images and with the problem's top-k MIL on real image-labelled abnormal images, never loading an expert mask.
A1-g0-C4.research_idea: Independent variable: synthetic-only, MIL-only and hybrid supervision. With probability 0.5, a normal source image receives a synthetic lesion (patch from another normal image of the same dataset, Poisson-blended, 1-10% of the foreground) and its mask is used with Dice + Focal; real abnormal images use top-k MIL (k = 1%); real normal images supervise all patches as normal. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities.
A1-g0-C4.hypothesis: Hybrid supervision exceeds both synthetic-only and MIL-only training by at least 1.5 held-out pixel-AUROC points and retains at least 80% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance.
A1-g0-C4.rationale: Synthetic anomalies come with exact masks at zero annotation cost, but alone they teach a model to find artefacts that look synthetic; real abnormal images with image labels carry realistic appearance but no location. A hybrid objective — Dice and Focal on synthetic anomalies, top-k MIL on real abnormal images — may give localisation that is both precise and realistic.
A1-g0-C4.method: 1) dataset/synthetic.py: wrapper around the training dataset that inserts synthetic lesions into normal images (p = 0.5) and returns their masks. 2) train_zero.py: seg loss = Focal + Dice on synthetic masks + lambda_MIL x topk_mil on real abnormal images (lambda_MIL = 1); real masks never loaded. 3) Hyper-parameters as released; lambda_MIL in {0.5, 1, 2}; insertion probability {0.25, 0.5}.
A1-g0-C4.experiment: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; synthetic-only; MIL-only. Falsified if hybrid is not better than both single-signal variants.
provenance: Fed-LoRA: Cross-Domain Generative Knowledge Feedback for Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g0-C5.title: Anatomy-debiased MIL: normal hard negatives and a positional normal prior
A1-g0-C5.summary: Make the problem's top-k MIL pick lesions rather than anatomy by (i) penalising the top-k patches of normal images and (ii) ranking abnormal-image patches after subtracting a running per-position mean of normal-image scores of the same dataset.
A1-g0-C5.research_idea: Independent variable: MIL variant (plain top-k MIL; + normal hard-negative top-k; + positional prior; both). For dataset d and level l, maintain an exponential moving average mu_dl(j) of patch anomaly probabilities of normal images at grid position j. Abnormal-image positive term: top-k (k = 1%) of p_j - mu_dl(j). Normal-image term: BCE towards 0 on all patches plus an extra weight 2 on the top-k patches. Dependent variables: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on held-out modalities; fraction of top-k patches that fall inside the true mask on masked source images (analysis).
A1-g0-C5.hypothesis: On held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, anatomy-debiased MIL increases pixel AUROC by at least 2 points and the fraction of selected top-k patches inside true lesions by at least 10 points compared with plain top-k MIL.
A1-g0-C5.rationale: Top-k MIL picks the patches with the highest anomaly score, and on medical images those are often anatomically salient structures (bright bone, vessels, the retinal layers) rather than lesions. ADAN shows such anatomy-driven activations dominate adapted CLIP maps. Two cheap corrections follow from image labels alone: mine the top-k patches of NORMAL images as hard negatives (they are anatomy, by definition), and subtract a per-dataset positional prior of normal anomaly scores before selecting the top-k of abnormal images.
A1-g0-C5.method: 1) loss.py: debiased_mil(p_l, label, dataset_id, ema_table, k_frac=0.01, w_hard=2). 2) train_zero.py: per-dataset EMA tables (6 x 4 levels x grid) updated with normal images (momentum 0.99); seg loss = debiased_mil at every level; detection branch unchanged. 3) The positional prior is used only during training; inference unchanged. 4) Hyper-parameters: k_frac 1%, w_hard {1, 2, 4}, EMA momentum 0.99.
A1-g0-C5.experiment: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; plain top-k MIL. Ablations: each component alone; w_hard; with/without the prior on ChestXray and HIS, where images are not spatially aligned. Falsified if neither component improves pixel AUROC over plain MIL.
provenance: Anatomic-Decoupling Adaptation: A Unified Framework for Zero/Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g0-C6.title: Is it the words or the frame? Anchor controls for MIL-trained segmentation adapters
A1-g0-C6.summary: Train the segmentation adapters with the problem's top-k MIL against three references — MVFA's text anchors, scale-matched random anchors, and a learned linear patch head — and test which property (meaning, fixed frame, scale) drives transfer of weakly supervised localisation.
A1-g0-C6.research_idea: Independent variable: patch-scoring reference during MIL training and testing (text anchors; random anchor pair with the same difference-vector length; random pair with 0.5x and 2x length; learned linear head, i.e. a learnable difference vector). Dependent variables: held-out pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC; plus the same comparison with mask supervision, so the effect of weak supervision and of the reference can be separated.
A1-g0-C6.hypothesis: Under top-k MIL, scale-matched random anchors reach held-out pixel AUROC within 1 point of MVFA's text anchors, while breaking the scale match (0.5x, 2x) reduces it by at least 2 points, and the learned linear head transfers worse than any fixed frame.
A1-g0-C6.rationale: The problem's hypothesis credits transfer of MIL-learned localisation to text anchors shared by all modalities. Do Words Matter? predicts that what is shared is a fixed coordinate frame and its scale, not linguistic content. This makes the hypothesis sharper and testable: if transfer comes from a fixed frame, scale-matched random anchors should localise as well as text anchors under MIL, and a per-modality learned head (no shared frame) should transfer worse.
A1-g0-C6.method: 1) utils.py: make_anchors(kind, seed): text (as released), random (Gaussian, normalised, difference rescaled to the text pair's difference length), scaled variants. 2) loss.py: topk_mil as in the problem. 3) train_zero.py: flag --anchors {text, rand, rand05, rand2, learned}; for 'learned' a 768-d difference vector is an nn.Parameter initialised to the text difference. 4) test_zero.py uses the same anchors as training. 5) Hyper-parameters as released; 3 random-anchor draws per seed.
A1-g0-C6.experiment: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA with text anchors and with scale-matched random anchors. Falsified if random anchors lose more than 2 points to text anchors under MIL (meaning matters) or if the learned head transfers as well as the fixed frames (frame does not matter).
provenance: Do Words Matter? What Text Contributes to Few and Full-Shot Vision-Language Anomaly Detection

A1-g1-o1.title: Cross-level consensus MIL: choosing instances by agreement of the four adapter levels
A1-g1-o1.summary: Select the positive instances of an abnormal image as the patches on which all four segmentation levels agree (geometric mean of level probabilities) and apply the MIL loss to those patches at every level, in a single training stage.
A1-g1-o1.hypothesis: Training MVFA's segmentation adapters with consensus MIL — top-k (k = 1%) selected on the geometric mean of the four level maps rather than per level — raises held-out pixel AUROC by at least 2 points and AUPRO by at least 3 points over per-level top-k MIL, because single-level top-k selections disagree and each level reinforces its own spurious maxima.
A1-g1-o1.rationale: The self-distillation parent shows that cross-level agreement filters noisy evidence, but uses it only after training, in a second stage that can lock in errors. The anchor-frame parent shows that all four levels read their patches in the same fixed anchor frame, so their probabilities are directly comparable across levels. Together they suggest a different mechanism: use cross-level agreement inside the MIL loss itself, as the instance selector. Per-level top-k lets each level pick its own (often anatomical) maxima; a consensus selector picks only patches that every level finds anomalous, which are more likely to be lesions, and then trains every level on those patches. This is one-stage, needs no pseudo-masks, and is a direct modification of the problem's operator.
A1-g1-o1.method: 1) loss.py: consensus_mil(p_levels, label, k_frac=0.01): c = exp(mean_l log p_l) per patch; idx = topk(c); positive loss for abnormal images = mean over levels of BCE(mean(p_l[idx]), 1); normal images: BCE(top-k mean of p_l, 0) per level as in the problem. 2) train_zero.py: replace the problem's per-level top-k MIL with consensus_mil; selection indices are detached. 3) Hyper-parameters: k_frac {0.5%, 1%, 2%}; consensus by geometric mean (ablation: minimum over levels); released learning rate and epochs. 4) Inference unchanged.
A1-g1-o1.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Ablations: geometric mean vs. minimum; consensus over levels 2-4 only. Diagnostics: overlap of per-level top-k selections; fraction of selected patches inside true masks on masked source images. Falsified if consensus MIL does not beat per-level MIL in AUPRO.
provenance: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection
Do Words Matter? What Text Contributes to Few and Full-Shot Vision-Language Anomaly Detection

A1-g1-o2.title: Normal-bank-gated MIL: selecting abnormal instances by distance to normal source patches
A1-g1-o2.summary: Replace the positional normal prior of anatomy-debiased MIL with a feature-space prior: rank the patches of an abnormal image by anomaly probability times their distance to a bank of normal patches of the same source dataset, so salient but normal anatomy is not selected — without assuming spatial alignment.
A1-g1-o2.hypothesis: Gating the top-k selection of MIL by the distance to the nearest normal source patch raises held-out pixel AUROC by at least 2 points over plain top-k MIL on all three masked held-out modalities, and, unlike the positional prior, does not reduce image AUROC on ChestXray and HIS by more than 0.5 points.
A1-g1-o2.rationale: The central component of the parent — a per-position running mean of normal scores — fails where images are not aligned (ChestXray crops, histopathology tiles). Its purpose is to discount patches that look anomalous only because they are salient normal anatomy. A feature-space substitute achieves the same without alignment: anatomy that occurs in normal images has close neighbours in a bank of normal patches of the same dataset (the mechanism MVFA's own few-shot branch uses at test time), while lesions do not. Using the bank only to choose MIL instances, not as a target, keeps the problem framing (image labels only), the quantity targeted (localisation by the segmentation adapters) and the evaluation.
A1-g1-o2.method: 1) build_normal_bank.py: per source dataset, frozen CLIP level-4 patch features of up to 500 normal training images, subsampled by greedy coreset to 20,000 vectors. 2) loss.py: gated_mil(p_l, feats, label, bank_d, k_frac=0.01): g_j = 1 - max cos(f_j, bank_d) (detached); select top-k by p_j * g_j; positive BCE on the mean p of selected patches; normal images: top-k BCE towards 0 with weight 2 (hard negatives, kept from the parent). 3) train_zero.py: use gated_mil at every level. 4) Hyper-parameters: bank size {5k, 20k}; k_frac 1%. Training-only; inference unchanged.
A1-g1-o2.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: plain top-k MIL; anatomy-debiased MIL with positional prior. Diagnostic: fraction of selected patches inside true masks on masked source images. Falsified if gating does not improve pixel AUROC over plain MIL.
provenance: Anatomic-Decoupling Adaptation: A Unified Framework for Zero/Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection
MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g1-o3.title: Equivariance-regularised MIL: dense self-supervision from geometric transforms
A1-g1-o3.summary: Densify the sparse MIL signal by requiring the segmentation maps of an image and of its flipped/rotated/cropped copy to agree after inverse transformation, using no pseudo-masks and no extra backbone.
A1-g1-o3.hypothesis: Adding a transformation-equivariance consistency loss (weight 1.0) to top-k MIL increases held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points and reduces the number of connected components per abnormal map by at least 30%, matching or exceeding two-stage pseudo-mask refinement without its extra stage.
A1-g1-o3.rationale: Both parents densify MIL supervision through an external target — pseudo-masks from the model itself or DINOv2 affinities — and both add a stage whose errors are frozen into the next. A different source of dense supervision is available in every image: a lesion moves with the image under flips, small rotations and crops, so the correct anomaly map is equivariant. Requiring the predicted maps of two views to agree after alignment constrains every patch, not only the top-k, and spreads MIL evidence over the whole lesion without any target map. It is a single-stage, single-backbone change.
A1-g1-o3.method: 1) train_zero.py: for each image draw a transform T (horizontal flip, rotation in [-15, 15] degrees, random resized crop 0.8-1.0); forward both x and T(x) through the seg branch. 2) loss.py: equi_loss = mean over levels of || T(p_l(x)) - p_l(T(x)) ||_1 over valid (overlapping) pixels, stop-gradient on neither. 3) Total seg loss = top-k MIL (problem) + 1.0 x equi_loss. 4) Hyper-parameters: weight {0.3, 1, 3}; transform family ablation. Training cost roughly doubles per step; epochs as released.
A1-g1-o3.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines also include two-stage MIL-to-mask self-distillation. Metrics: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, connected components per map, image AUROC. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over MIL alone.
provenance: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection
Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

A1-g1-o4.title: Counterfactual occlusion targets: teaching the segmentation adapters what the image-label detector needs
A1-g1-o4.summary: Use MVFA's image-label-trained detection branch as a counterfactual oracle: the patches whose occlusion (replacement by matched normal tissue) most lowers its image score form the training target of the segmentation adapters, so localisation is learned from causal evidence rather than from the highest-scoring patches.
A1-g1-o4.hypothesis: Segmentation adapters trained on occlusion-sensitivity targets of the detection branch achieve at least 3 points higher held-out AUPRO than top-k MIL and retain at least 75% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance, because occlusion sensitivity selects patches that cause the abnormal label instead of patches that merely score high.
A1-g1-o4.rationale: Every MIL variant — symmetric, asymmetric or sigmoid — chooses instances by correlation: the highest-scoring patches. In medical images these are often salient anatomy. A different principle is counterfactual: a patch is part of the lesion if removing it turns the image normal. MVFA already has a detector trained on image labels for all five source datasets (its detection branch, mean-pooled BCE in the released code). Occluding blocks of an abnormal image by inpainting them with the nearest normal-bank patches and measuring the drop of the detector's score gives a dense, image-label-only target map. Unlike pseudo-mask self-distillation, the target comes from a different branch and a different question (necessity), so the segmentation adapters do not reinforce their own maxima.
A1-g1-o4.method: 1) Stage 1: train MVFA as released but with segmentation loss off (detection branch only, image labels from all five source datasets). 2) occlusion_targets.py (offline, once per fold): for each abnormal source image, split the grid into 4x4-patch blocks (about 20 blocks); for each block replace its patch tokens at the input layer by those of the nearest normal-bank patches (frozen CLIP features, same dataset) and record the drop of the detector's image score; normalise drops to [0, 1] per image; normal images get zero maps. 3) Stage 2: train the segmentation adapters with a soft BCE on the occlusion targets (abnormal images) plus all-patches-normal BCE (normal images). 4) Hyper-parameters: block size {2x2, 4x4}; target temperature; released learning rate and epochs. Cost: about 20 forward passes per abnormal source image, done once.
A1-g1-o4.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: top-k MIL; detection-branch maps used directly as segmentation output. Ablations: block size; occlusion by normal-bank patches vs. by mean token. Diagnostic: Spearman correlation of occlusion targets with true masks on masked source images. Falsified if AUPRO does not exceed top-k MIL.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Do Words Matter? What Text Contributes to Few and Full-Shot Vision-Language Anomaly Detection

A1-g1-o5.title: Anatomy-debiased MIL under text and random anchor frames
A1-g1-o5.summary: Train the segmentation adapters with top-k MIL plus hard-negative mining of the top-k patches of normal images, under MVFA's text anchors and under scale-matched random anchors, to test both whether debiasing improves weak localisation and whether its effect depends on the meaning of the anchors.
A1-g1-o5.hypothesis: Normal hard-negative mining raises held-out pixel AUROC of MIL-trained segmentation adapters by at least 2 points over plain top-k MIL, and the gain is the same (within 1 point) under text and scale-matched random anchors, showing that it acts on the visual adapters rather than on anchor semantics.
A1-g1-o5.rationale: The anatomy parent identifies a concrete failure of MIL (top-k patches on salient anatomy) and corrects it with image labels alone; its positional prior is fragile on unaligned modalities, so only the hard-negative term is kept, which needs no alignment. The anchor-frame parent provides the control that separates the contribution of text meaning from that of a fixed frame and its scale. Combining them gives one improvement and one explanation in a 2 x 2 design whose cells are each one flag in the training script.
A1-g1-o5.method: 1) loss.py: mil_hardneg(p_l, label, k_frac=0.01, w_hard=2): abnormal images: BCE(top-k mean, 1); normal images: BCE on all patches towards 0 plus w_hard x BCE(top-k mean, 0). 2) utils.py: make_anchors('text' | 'rand'), random pair rescaled to the text pair's difference length, 3 draws. 3) train_zero.py: flags --loss {mil, mil_hardneg} --anchors {text, rand}. 4) Hyper-parameters: w_hard {1, 2, 4}; released learning rate and epochs.
A1-g1-o5.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. 2 x 2 design (loss x anchors) plus mask-supervised MVFA with text anchors. Diagnostic: fraction of top-k patches of abnormal source images inside true masks. Falsified if hard negatives do not improve pixel AUROC, or if their gain differs by more than 1 point between frames.
provenance: Anatomic-Decoupling Adaptation: A Unified Framework for Zero/Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection
Do Words Matter? What Text Contributes to Few and Full-Shot Vision-Language Anomaly Detection

A1-g1-o6.title: Witness-rate-adaptive MIL: estimating each dataset's lesion fraction by positive-unlabelled mixture-proportion estimation
A1-g1-o6.summary: Replace the fixed k = 1% of the MIL operator by a per-dataset witness rate estimated from image labels alone — the fraction of patches in abnormal images whose scores are not explained by the normal-image score distribution — and update it during training.
A1-g1-o6.hypothesis: Per-dataset witness-rate-adaptive k improves held-out pixel AUROC by at least 1.5 points over the best single fixed k chosen on source validation, and the estimated witness rates rank the three masked source datasets in the same order as their true median lesion areas.
A1-g1-o6.rationale: The asymmetric-MIL parent and the problem both fix k, yet BMAD's lesions range from small retinal fluid pockets to large brain tumours and diffuse chest findings, so any single k is wrong for most datasets. Positive-unlabelled learning offers an analogous principle: patches of abnormal images are an unlabelled mixture of normal and lesion patches, and patches of normal images are a clean sample of the normal component. The mixture proportion (the witness rate) can be estimated from the two score distributions (for example by the best-bin estimator of Scott, 2015) and used as k for that dataset. No masks are needed, and the estimate is checkable against the masks that do exist.
A1-g1-o6.method: 1) loss.py: topk_mil with per-dataset k_d. 2) train_zero.py: every 2 epochs, on a held-out portion of each source dataset, collect level-4 patch probabilities of normal and abnormal images; estimate pi_d = min over thresholds t of (1 - F_abn(t))/(1 - F_norm(t)) (best-bin estimator, upper-bounded by 0.5); set k_d = max(3 patches, pi_d x number of patches); first 2 epochs use k = 1%. 3) Hyper-parameters: update interval 2 epochs; clipping [0.5%, 30%]. Inference unchanged.
A1-g1-o6.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: fixed k in {0.5%, 1%, 5%} chosen on source validation; asymmetric sigmoid MIL. Diagnostic: estimated pi_d vs. true mask area fraction on BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Falsified if adaptive k does not beat the best fixed k.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g2-o1.title: Matched-pair MIL ranking: borrowing the ranking objective of weakly supervised video anomaly detection
A1-g2-o1.summary: Train the segmentation adapters with a ranking loss that requires the most anomalous patches of an abnormal image to score above the most anomalous patches of its most similar normal image from the same dataset, instead of pushing absolute probabilities to 0 and 1.
A1-g2-o1.hypothesis: A matched-pair hinge ranking loss between the top-k patches of an abnormal image and those of its nearest normal image (CLS similarity, same dataset) yields at least 2 points higher held-out pixel AUROC than top-k BCE MIL, because a relative constraint against matched anatomy does not reward salient normal structures that both images share.
A1-g2-o1.rationale: Weakly supervised video anomaly detection learns frame-level localisation from video-level labels with a MIL ranking loss: the highest-scoring segment of an anomalous video must outrank the highest-scoring segment of a normal video. The analogous principle applies to MVFA's patch maps, with one improvement available in medical data: pairing each abnormal image with the most similar normal image of the same dataset. Anatomy that both images share then cancels in the ranking, so the loss only rewards patches that are anomalous relative to matched normal anatomy — the failure mode that per-image top-k BCE and witness-rate tuning cannot remove.
A1-g2-o1.method: 1) precompute_pairs.py: per source dataset, frozen CLIP CLS embeddings; for each abnormal training image its 5 nearest normal images. 2) loss.py: rank_mil(p_abn, p_nor, k_frac=0.01, margin=0.2) = max(0, margin - topk_mean(p_abn) + topk_mean(p_nor)) + 1e-3 x smoothness (sum of squared differences of neighbouring patches) + 1e-3 x sparsity (mean p_abn), per level as in Sultani et al. 3) train_zero.py: batches contain an abnormal image and one of its matched normals (random among the 5); normal images also receive top-k BCE towards 0. 4) Hyper-parameters: margin {0.1, 0.2, 0.5}; released learning rate and epochs.
A1-g2-o1.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: top-k BCE MIL; ranking with random (unmatched) normal pairs. Falsified if matched ranking does not beat top-k BCE MIL, or if unmatched pairs work as well (pairing does not matter).
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Anatomic-Decoupling Adaptation: A Unified Framework for Zero/Few-Shot Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g2-o2.title: Mosaic MIL: free quadrant labels from four-image mosaics
A1-g2-o2.summary: Create training mosaics of four down-scaled source images (normal and abnormal, same dataset) whose quadrant labels are known from the image labels, and train the segmentation adapters to localise abnormality at quadrant level together with consensus MIL inside abnormal quadrants.
A1-g2-o2.hypothesis: Adding mosaic training (50% of batches) to consensus MIL raises held-out pixel AUROC by at least 2 points, because quadrant-level supervision forces the segmentation maps to discriminate where in an image the abnormality is, which image-level losses on single images never require.
A1-g2-o2.rationale: Consensus MIL improves which patches are selected, but every loss on a single image is satisfied by raising one image-wide score, so maps need never be spatially discriminative. A mosaic changes the task without any annotation: the label of each quadrant is the label of the image placed there, so a mosaic carries coarse localisation labels for free. Patches of normal quadrants are pixel-level negatives in an image that also contains a lesion — exactly the hard negatives MIL lacks — and consensus MIL is applied inside each abnormal quadrant.
A1-g2-o2.method: 1) dataset/mosaic.py: with probability 0.5 build a 2x2 mosaic of four images from one source dataset (each resized to 120x120), with 1-3 abnormal quadrants; quadrant label map. 2) loss.py: mosaic_loss: BCE towards 0 on every patch of normal quadrants; consensus top-k MIL (k = 1% of quadrant patches) inside each abnormal quadrant. 3) train_zero.py: seg loss = consensus MIL on single images + mosaic_loss on mosaics. 4) Hyper-parameters: mosaic probability {0.25, 0.5}; quadrant size 120 px. Inference unchanged.
A1-g2-o2.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: consensus MIL; per-level MIL. Ablation: mosaics with only normal or only abnormal quadrants (no spatial contrast). Falsified if mosaic training does not improve pixel AUROC.
provenance: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g2-o3.title: Consensus MIL with an anchor-frame control
A1-g2-o3.summary: Train the segmentation adapters with cross-level consensus MIL under MVFA's text anchors and under scale-matched random anchors, testing whether consensus selection improves weak localisation and whether its benefit relies on the shared anchor frame rather than on the anchors' meaning.
A1-g2-o3.hypothesis: Consensus MIL (top-k on the geometric mean of the four level maps) raises held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points over per-level MIL under both text and scale-matched random anchors, with a difference of less than 1 point between the two frames, whereas giving each level its own random frame removes at least half of the consensus gain.
A1-g2-o3.rationale: The consensus parent argues that the four levels' probabilities are comparable because they are read in one anchor frame; the anchor-control parent shows, following Do Words Matter?, that this frame matters through its geometry, not its words. Combining them makes the mechanism of consensus MIL testable: if the shared frame is what makes level agreement meaningful, scale-matched random anchors should work as well as text anchors, and separate random frames per level should break the consensus gain.
A1-g2-o3.method: 1) loss.py: consensus_mil as in the parent (geometric mean of level probabilities, top-k = 1%, selection detached; normal images: per-level top-k BCE towards 0). 2) utils.py: make_anchors('text' | 'rand' | 'rand_per_level'), random pairs rescaled to the text pair's difference length, 3 draws. 3) train_zero.py: flags --loss {mil, consensus} --anchors {text, rand, rand_per_level}. 4) Hyper-parameters: k_frac 1%; released learning rate and epochs.
A1-g2-o3.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Design: loss {per-level MIL, consensus} x anchors {text, shared random, per-level random}. Diagnostics: overlap of per-level top-k sets; fraction of selected patches inside true masks. Falsified if consensus does not beat per-level MIL, or if per-level random frames keep the full gain.

A1-g2-o4.title: Posterior-weighted MIL: a two-component mixture of patch scores replaces hard top-k selection
A1-g2-o4.summary: Keep the witness-rate framing but replace hard top-k selection with soft per-patch weights: a two-component mixture fitted per dataset on patch scores, with the normal component fixed from normal images, gives every patch of an abnormal image a posterior probability of being lesion, used as its target weight.
A1-g2-o4.hypothesis: Posterior-weighted MIL increases held-out AUPRO by at least 2 points over witness-rate-adaptive top-k MIL, and its fitted mixing proportions correlate (Spearman >= 0.8 over masked source datasets and epochs) with true lesion area fractions.
A1-g2-o4.rationale: The parent's core component — a mixture-proportion estimate turned into a hard k — discards which patches are likely lesions beyond the top-k cut and is sensitive to the estimator's noise. A two-component mixture model of patch scores (normal component estimated from normal images, lesion component free) gives both the proportion and a per-patch posterior. Using the posterior as a soft target keeps the problem's framing (image labels only), the quantity targeted (localisation by the segmentation adapters) and the evaluation, and degrades gracefully when the components overlap.
A1-g2-o4.method: 1) Every 2 epochs, per source dataset and level: fit a kernel density f0 to logit patch scores of normal images; fit pi and a Gaussian f1 to abnormal-image patch scores by EM with f0 fixed. 2) Posterior w_j = pi f1(s_j) / (pi f1(s_j) + (1 - pi) f0(s_j)). 3) loss.py: post_mil: abnormal images: weighted BCE with targets w_j (detached) on all patches; normal images: BCE towards 0 on all patches. 4) First 2 epochs: plain top-k MIL to obtain informative scores. 5) Hyper-parameters: refit interval 2 epochs; pi clipped to [0.005, 0.3].
A1-g2-o4.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: witness-rate-adaptive top-k MIL; fixed top-k MIL. Diagnostics: fitted pi vs. true lesion area fraction; posterior AUROC against masks on source images. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over witness-rate top-k MIL.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP
Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g2-o5.title: Co-teaching MIL between MVFA's detection and segmentation adapters
A1-g2-o5.summary: Let MVFA's two adapter sets select instances for each other: the detection branch's patch map (trained on all images with image labels) chooses the top-k patches on which the segmentation branch's MIL loss is applied, and vice versa, so neither branch reinforces its own spurious maxima.
A1-g2-o5.hypothesis: Cross-branch instance selection raises held-out pixel AUROC of the segmentation branch by at least 2 points over self-selected consensus MIL and reduces the fraction of selected patches on salient normal anatomy (measured on masked source images) by at least 10 points.
A1-g2-o5.rationale: Consensus MIL relies on agreement between levels of the same branch, whose errors are correlated because they share training signal. Co-teaching, a principle from learning with noisy labels, uses two networks that select training instances for each other because their errors differ. MVFA already contains two networks of this kind: the detection adapters and the segmentation adapters, separate parameter sets on the same backbone, trained with different losses. Exchanging their top-k selections is a small change that exploits this existing architecture.
A1-g2-o5.method: 1) loss.py: cross_mil(p_seg, p_det, label, k_frac=0.01): idx_seg = topk(p_det) (detached) for the seg loss; idx_det = topk(p_seg) (detached) for an added det-branch top-k term; normal images: top-k BCE towards 0 in both branches. 2) train_zero.py: det branch keeps its mean-pooled BCE and adds the cross term with weight 0.5; seg branch uses cross_mil. 3) Warm-up: 2 epochs of self-selection. 4) Hyper-parameters: k_frac 1%; cross-term weight {0.25, 0.5, 1}.
A1-g2-o5.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: consensus MIL; per-level MIL. Diagnostics: overlap of the two branches' selections over training; fraction of selected patches inside true masks. Falsified if cross-selection does not beat consensus MIL.
provenance: Fine-Tuning CLIP Models with Convolutional Features for Medical Anomaly Detection

A1-g2-o6.title: Distilling a normal-bank novelty map into the segmentation adapters alongside MIL
A1-g2-o6.summary: Give the segmentation adapters a dense, label-free auxiliary target on every source image — the distance of each patch to a bank of normal patches of the same dataset — and combine it with image-level MIL, so localisation is shaped everywhere rather than only at the top-k.
A1-g2-o6.hypothesis: Adding a novelty-distillation regression term (weight 0.5) to MIL raises held-out AUPRO by at least 3 points over normal-bank-gated MIL, and the gain persists when the bank is restricted to 1,000 patches per dataset.
A1-g2-o6.rationale: The gated-MIL parent uses the normal bank only to choose a handful of instances. The bank supports a stronger, dense signal: its patch-wise novelty map (as in PatchCore) is a reasonable unsupervised localisation of abnormal tissue for every patch of every image, including normal images. Distilling this map into the segmentation adapters gives dense supervision; the MIL term with image labels then corrects the novelty map where unusual but normal anatomy is novel. The bank is used only during training, so test-time behaviour and cost remain MVFA's.
A1-g2-o6.method: 1) build_normal_bank.py (as in the parent): per dataset coreset of normal level-4 patch features. 2) Target n_j = 1 - max cos(f_j, bank_d), excluding patches of the same image for normal images; standardised per dataset to [0, 1] by 1st/99th percentiles. 3) loss.py: L = gated top-k MIL + 0.5 x mean_j (p_j - n_j)^2 on all images (all levels). 4) Hyper-parameters: weight {0.25, 0.5, 1}; bank size {1k, 20k}. Inference unchanged.
A1-g2-o6.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: normal-bank-gated MIL; novelty map alone used as the segmentation output (PatchCore-style). Falsified if AUPRO does not exceed gated MIL.

A1-g3-o1.title: Learnable log-sum-exp pooling per dataset replaces fixed top-k in MIL
A1-g3-o1.summary: Replace the hard top-k mean of the MIL operator by log-sum-exp pooling with a learnable temperature per source dataset, which interpolates smoothly between max and mean pooling and lets gradient descent find each dataset's effective lesion fraction from image labels.
A1-g3-o1.hypothesis: Per-dataset learnable log-sum-exp pooling matches or exceeds witness-rate-adaptive top-k MIL in held-out pixel AUROC (difference >= 0) and the learned temperatures order the masked source datasets by their true lesion area fraction.
A1-g3-o1.rationale: Witness-rate MIL estimates the lesion fraction outside the network with a statistical estimator and then applies a hard cut. An analogous but end-to-end principle exists in weakly supervised localisation: smooth pooling operators whose sharpness is a parameter. With a learnable temperature r_d per dataset, LSE pooling (1/r) log mean exp(r p_j) behaves like max pooling for large r and like mean pooling for small r, so the image-level loss itself learns how concentrated each dataset's lesions are. Every patch receives gradient in proportion to its softmax weight, which also avoids the discontinuity of top-k.
A1-g3-o1.method: 1) loss.py: lse_pool(p, r) = (1/r) log(mean_j exp(r p_j)); r_d = softplus(rho_d) + 1, rho_d learnable per source dataset (init so that r = 20). 2) MIL loss: BCE(lse_pool(p_l, r_d), y) per level for every image (normal images included). 3) train_zero.py: rho_d in the seg optimizer. 4) On the held-out modality, r is not needed at test time (inference unchanged). Hyper-parameters: init r {5, 20, 50}.
A1-g3-o1.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: fixed top-k MIL; witness-rate top-k MIL. Diagnostic: learned r_d vs. true lesion area fraction. Falsified if LSE pooling is worse than witness-rate top-k.
provenance: MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP

A1-g3-o2.title: Per-image adaptive k from normal-bank exceedances
A1-g3-o2.summary: Set the MIL instance count of each abnormal image to the number of its patches whose distance to a bank of normal patches of the same dataset exceeds the 99th percentile of normal-image distances, so k follows the lesion size of that image rather than a fixed or per-dataset value.
A1-g3-o2.hypothesis: Per-image k from normal-bank exceedances raises held-out pixel AUROC by at least 1.5 points over per-dataset witness-rate k and by at least 2 points over fixed k = 1%, and the per-image k correlates with true lesion area on masked source images (Spearman >= 0.5).
A1-g3-o2.rationale: The gated-MIL parent uses a normal bank to decide which patches to select; the witness-rate parent decides how many, but only per dataset. Lesion size varies strongly within a dataset (small and large tumours in BrainMRI, small and large fluid regions in RESC), so the right k is a property of the image. Counting the patches that are novel relative to the normal bank gives a label-free, per-image estimate of how many patches the lesion occupies; selection by anomaly score then trains the adapters on that many patches.
A1-g3-o2.method: 1) build_normal_bank.py: per dataset, coreset of frozen level-4 normal patch features; threshold t_d = 99th percentile of leave-one-image-out distances of normal patches. 2) loss.py: k_i = clip(#{j: 1 - max cos(f_j, bank_d) > t_d}, 3, 30% of patches) for abnormal images (computed once per epoch, detached); MIL positive term = BCE(top-k_i mean of p, 1); normal images: top-k BCE towards 0 with k = 1%. 3) train_zero.py: per-image k used at every level. Inference unchanged.
A1-g3-o2.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: fixed k; per-dataset witness-rate k; gated MIL. Diagnostic: Spearman correlation of k_i with true lesion area on masked source images. Falsified if per-image k is not better than per-dataset k.

A1-g3-o3.title: Mosaic MIL with normal-bank-gated instance selection
A1-g3-o3.summary: Train the segmentation adapters on four-image mosaics whose normal quadrants are pixel-level negatives, and select the positive instances inside abnormal quadrants by anomaly probability gated by distance to a normal-patch bank, so both the spatial contrast and the instance choice avoid normal anatomy.
A1-g3-o3.hypothesis: Gated mosaic MIL raises held-out pixel AUROC by at least 1.5 points over mosaic MIL with plain consensus selection and by at least 3 points over single-image top-k MIL.
A1-g3-o3.rationale: Mosaic MIL contributes free spatial contrast (normal quadrants as negatives); gated MIL contributes alignment-free debiasing of instance selection. Their failure modes are complementary: mosaics still select instances by raw score inside abnormal quadrants, and gated MIL never sees an image in which normal and abnormal regions coexist with known labels. Combining them addresses both in one single-stage loss.
A1-g3-o3.method: 1) build_normal_bank.py as in gated MIL. 2) dataset/mosaic.py as in mosaic MIL. 3) loss.py: inside each abnormal quadrant select top-k (1% of quadrant patches) by p_j x g_j with g_j = 1 - max cos(f_j, bank_d) (detached); BCE towards 0 on all patches of normal quadrants; single images use gated MIL. 4) train_zero.py: mosaic probability 0.5. Inference unchanged.
A1-g3-o3.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: mosaic MIL; gated MIL; top-k MIL. Falsified if gated mosaic MIL does not beat both parents.

A1-g3-o4.title: Mosaic-to-single-image map consistency
A1-g3-o4.summary: Keep the mosaic framing but replace the label-proportion (mass) consistency with dense map consistency: the segmentation map of each quadrant of a mosaic must equal the map of its source image computed alone at the same resolution.
A1-g3-o4.hypothesis: Dense mosaic-to-single map consistency reduces relative lesion-area error by at least 25% and raises AUPRO by at least 2 points over mosaic MIL, at least matching the label-proportion loss on both metrics.
A1-g3-o4.rationale: The parent's core component constrains only a scalar (total abnormal mass) per mosaic. Its purpose — making the adapters' maps independent of context so that area is consistent — is served more directly by requiring that each quadrant's map in the mosaic equals the map of the same image seen alone. This dense constraint uses the same forward passes, keeps the problem framing (image labels only), targets the same quantity (map area and shape) and keeps the evaluation.
A1-g3-o4.method: 1) dataset/mosaic.py as in the parent. 2) Forward the four source images individually at 120 px (stop-gradient) and the mosaic. 3) loss.py: cons = mean over quadrants and levels of || p(mosaic)[quadrant q] - p(image_q) ||_1, plus BCE towards 0 on normal quadrants and consensus MIL inside abnormal quadrants. 4) Hyper-parameters: consistency weight {0.5, 1}; mosaic probability 0.5. Inference unchanged.
A1-g3-o4.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: mosaic MIL; label-proportion mosaic MIL. Metrics: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, relative lesion-area error. Falsified if dense consistency is not at least as good as the mass consistency.

A1-g3-o5.title: MPE-anchored posterior MIL
A1-g3-o5.summary: Fix the mixing proportion of the posterior-weighted MIL mixture to the witness rate estimated by positive-unlabelled mixture-proportion estimation, and fit only the lesion component, which makes the per-patch posteriors stable early in training while keeping soft targets.
A1-g3-o5.hypothesis: Anchoring the mixture proportion to the MPE estimate reduces the epoch-to-epoch variation of the fitted lesion posterior by at least 50% and raises held-out AUPRO by at least 1 point over free-proportion posterior MIL.
A1-g3-o5.rationale: The witness-rate parent estimates the proportion of lesion patches robustly but uses it only as a hard k; the posterior parent uses soft targets but must estimate proportion and lesion component jointly, which is unstable when the two distributions overlap early in training. Using the MPE estimate as the fixed proportion and fitting only the lesion component combines the robust part of one with the soft targets of the other.
A1-g3-o5.method: 1) Every 2 epochs per source dataset and level: pi_d from the best-bin MPE estimator; f0 from normal-image patch scores (kernel density); f1 Gaussian fitted by EM with pi fixed to pi_d. 2) Posterior weights as in posterior MIL; weighted BCE for abnormal images; BCE towards 0 for normal images. 3) First 2 epochs: top-k MIL. Hyper-parameters: refit interval 2 epochs; pi clip [0.005, 0.3].
A1-g3-o5.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: posterior MIL with free proportion; witness-rate top-k MIL. Diagnostics: posterior stability across epochs; posterior AUROC against masks on source images. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over free-proportion posterior MIL.

A1-g3-o6.title: Feature-space anomaly mixing: graded synthetic positives from normal-bank patches
A1-g3-o6.summary: Create synthetic training patches in feature space by mixing the features of normal-bank patches with those of the gated top patches of abnormal images at random ratios, and train the segmentation adapters to output the mixing ratio, giving dense, graded patch-level supervision without image-space artefacts.
A1-g3-o6.hypothesis: Adding feature-space mixing (weight 0.5) to gated MIL raises held-out AUPRO by at least 2 points over gated MIL alone, and outperforms image-space synthetic lesions (Poisson blending) under the same training budget.
A1-g3-o6.rationale: Gated MIL selects a few positive patches per abnormal image and leaves most of the map unsupervised. Image-space synthetic lesions add supervision but teach the model blending artefacts. An analogous trick from representation learning (mixup in feature space) avoids both: a convex combination of a normal patch feature and a likely-lesion patch feature at ratio lambda is a patch whose abnormality is known to be lambda, and such graded examples shape the adapters' output scale over the whole range, not only at 0 and 1. Because mixing happens at the input of the adapter at each level, it needs no new images and no masks.
A1-g3-o6.method: 1) Per batch and level: take the gated top-k patch features of abnormal images (as in gated MIL) and an equal number of random normal-bank patch features of the same dataset. 2) Mixed feature f_mix = lambda f_abn + (1 - lambda) f_nor with lambda ~ U(0, 1); pass through the level's segmentation adapter. 3) loss.py: mix_loss = BCE(p(f_mix), lambda) (soft target) added to gated MIL with weight 0.5. 4) Hyper-parameters: weight {0.25, 0.5, 1}; number of mixed patches per batch 64. Inference unchanged.
A1-g3-o6.experiment: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: gated MIL; gated MIL + image-space synthetic lesions. Falsified if feature mixing does not improve AUPRO over gated MIL.
